name: /Xam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: /Xam (xamm1241, Tuu, extinct) is not in the catalog. The single works with stress in the title, Schmidt 1986 'Tales and beliefs about eyes-on-his-feet', is a Khoisan folklore chapter (Glottolog record read; the hit is the word 'feet' in a tale-character's name) and is irrelevant. No first-hand statement of /Xam word-stress placement was found in any open source: Bleek & Lloyd 1911 (preface pp. viii-ix) and D.F. Bleek 1956 (note under 'a') speak only of tone marks and 'variations in tone and length'; Bleek 1862's accent section covers Hottentot/Bantu only; Müller 1888's /Kham sketch has no Betonung paragraph; the Tumʔi descriptions (Kilian 2020/2022) say only that schwa is an 'unstressed central vowel' found in non-initial syllables. The likeliest deciding sources remain unread: D.F. Bleek 1928-30 'Bushman grammar' and Meriggi 1928-29 (both in ZES 19, HathiTrust full-view but could not be reached by automated download; not on archive.org), Traill 1995 (print only, Harvard offsite), and Güldemann's |Xam sections in Vossen 2013 'Phonetics and phonology' (doi 10.4324/9780203084465-12) and 'Tonology' (-13), paywalled. Acquisition priority high for all four. ( updated).org worked.

sources.citation: Kilian, Kelly. 2022. The phonological system of Tumʔi. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics Plus 64: 111-131. (and Kilian 2020, MA thesis, U. Calgary, hdl 1880/111508)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.quote: Finally, the phoneme /ə/ is articulated as an unstressed central vowel. The schwa in Tumʔi generally appears in the second or final syllable, only observed in the first syllable of [|qəri] honey beer, [pəri] 'goat', [məkəs] 'upper thighs', and Afrikaans loan words such as [vələ] 'wild' from the Afrikaans word 'wilde' (vəldə).
sources.locator: 2022 p. 118 (sect. on vowels); same wording in 2020 thesis ch. 3
sources.note: Sections 4-5 cover clicks, consonants, vowels, phonation; no suprasegmental/tone/stress section. Only mention: 'the phoneme /ə/ is articulated as an unstressed central vowel' (p. 118). Describes Tumʔi (Prieska), not 19th-c. |Xam.

sources.quote: The number of words of different meanings expressed by ă is surprising. Some variations in tone and length have been noted, doubtless others have not been heard and recorded. Still the number of meanings attached to the same sound is remarkable.
